patches.old:
As I sat at home, I praised the Lord for everything I had seen. I thought about the commandments: they are good and powerful, they bring joy, they are glorious, and they can save a person’s soul. I said to myself, “I will be blessed if I follow these commandments, and everyone who follows them will be blessed.”

While I was thinking about these things, I suddenly saw him sitting beside me. He said, “Why are you wavering about the commandments I gave you? They are good. Do not waver at all. Instead, clothe yourself with faith in the Lord, and you will follow them, for I will give you strength to do so.

“These commandments help those who are ready to repent[a]. But if they do not live by them, their repentance is useless.

“So, you who are turning away from your sins, throw off the evils of this age that wear you down. Clothe yourselves with every righteous virtue. Then you will be able to obey these commandments and stop adding to your sins. If you add no more sins, you will leave your former sins behind. Walk in these commandments of mine—follow them—and you will live for God. I have told you these things.”

After he had finished speaking with me, he said, “Let us go out into the countryside, and I will show you the shepherds who tend the sheep.”

“Let us go, sir,” I replied.

We came to a plain, where he showed me a young shepherd. The young man was wearing a saffron-colored outfit.

He was tending a very large flock of sheep. The sheep seemed to be living luxuriously and extravagantly. They were happy and leaped here and there. The shepherd was delighted with his flock. He looked extremely happy, and he ran about among the sheep.

All other wording, paragraph divisions, quotation prefixes, and the existing note marker remain unchanged.

translation:
  text: 'While I was sitting in my house and glorifying the Lord for all the things I had seen, and pondering
    the commandments—that they are good and powerful and gladdening and glorious and able to save a person’s
    soul—I said within myself: “Blessed shall I be if I walk in these commandments, and whoever walks
    in these will be blessed.”


    As I was saying these things within myself, I suddenly see him seated beside me and saying this: “Why
    are you double-minded about the commandments that I commanded you? They are good. Do not be double-minded
    at all, but clothe yourself with faith in the Lord, and you will walk in them; for I will strengthen
    you in them.


    “These commandments are beneficial for those who are about to repent[a]; for if they do not walk in
    them, their repentance is in vain.


    “You who are repenting, therefore, throw off the evils of this age that wear you down; and having
    put on every virtue of righteousness, you will be able to keep these commandments and no longer add
    to your sins. If, therefore, you add nothing further, you will be separated from your former sins.
    Walk, therefore, in these my commandments, and you will live to God. These things [all] have been
    spoken to you by me.”


    And after he had spoken these things with me, he says to me, “Let us go into a field, and I will show
    you the shepherds of the sheep.” “Let us go, sir,” I say. And we came to a certain plain, and he shows
    me a shepherd, a young man, clothed in a suit of garments, saffron in color.


    He was pasturing very many sheep, and the sheep were as if living in luxury and very self-indulgent,
    and they were cheerful, skipping here and there. And the shepherd himself was very cheerful over his
    flock; and the very appearance of the shepherd was exceedingly cheerful, and he ran around among the
    sheep.'
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted
      to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while
      preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance;
      do not impose a different tradition on it.
    reason: lexical_alternative

  text: Καθήμενος ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ μου καὶ δοξάζων τὸν Κύριον περὶ πάντων ὧν ἑωράκειν, καὶ συζητῶν περὶ τῶν
    ἐντολῶν, ὅτι καλαὶ καὶ δυναταὶ καὶ ἱλαραὶ καὶ ἔνδοξοι καὶ δυνάμεναι σῶσαι ψυχὴν ἀνθρώπου, ἔλεγον ἐν
    ἐμαυτῷ· Μακάριος ἔσομαι ἐὰν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς ταύταις πορευθῶ, καὶ ὃς ἂν ταύταις πορευθῇ, μακάριος ἔσται.
    2. ὡς ταῦτα ἐν ἐμαυτῷ ἐλάλουν, βλέπω αὐτὸν ἐξαίφνης παρακαθήμενόν μοι καὶ λέγοντα ταῦτα· Τί διψυχεῖς
    περὶ τῶν ἐντολῶν ὧν σοι ἐνετειλάμην; καλαί εἰσιν· ὅλως μὴ διψυχήσῃς, ἀλλ᾽ ἔνδυσαι τὴν πίστιν τοῦ Κυρίου,
    καὶ ἐν αὐταῖς πορεύσῃ· ἐγὼ γάρ σε ἐνδυναμώσω ἐν αὐταῖς. 3. αὗται αἱ ἐντολαὶ σύμφοροί εἰσι τοῖς μέλλουσι
    μετανοεῖν· ἐὰν γὰρ μὴ πορευθῶσιν ἐν αὐταῖς, εἰς μάτην ἐστὶν ἡ μετάνοια αὐτῶν. 4. οἱ οὖν μετανοοῦντες
    ἀποβάλλετε τὰς πονηρίας τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου τὰς ἐκτριβούσας ὑμᾶς· ἐνδυσάμενοι δὲ πᾶσαν ἀρετὴν δικαιοσύνης
    δυνήσεσθε τηρῆσαι τὰς ἐντολὰς ταύτας καὶ μηκέτι προστιθέναι ταῖς ἁμαρτίαις ὑμῶν. | ἐὰν οὖν μηκέτι
    μηδὲν προσθῆτε, ἀποστήσεσθε ἀπὸ τῶν προτέρων ἁμαρτιῶν ὑμῶν. | πορεύεσθε οὖν ταῖς ἐντολαῖς μου ταύταις,
    καὶ ζήσεσθε τῷ Θεῷ. ταῦτα [πάντα] παρ' ἐμοῦ λελάληται ὑμῖν. 5. καὶ μετὰ τὸ ταῦτα λαλῆσαι αὐτὸν μετ'
    ἐμοῦ, λέγει μοι· Ἄγωμεν εἰς ἀγρόν, καὶ δείξω σοι τοὺς ποιμένας τῶν προβάτων. Ἄγωμεν, φημί, κύριε.
    καὶ ἤλθομεν εἴς τι πεδίον, καὶ δεικνύει μοι ποιμένα νεανίσκον ἐνδεδυμένον σύνθεσιν ἱματίων, τῷ χρώματι
    κροκώδη. 6. ἔβοσκε δὲ πρόβατα πολλὰ λίαν, καὶ τὰ πρόβατα ταῦτα ὡσεὶ τρυφῶντα ἦν καὶ λίαν σπαταλῶντα,
    καὶ ἱλαρὰ ἦν σκιρτῶντα ὧδε κἀκεῖ· καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ ποιμὴν πάνυ ἱλαρὸς ἦν ἐπὶ τῷ ποιμνίῳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ αὐτὴ
    ἡ ἰδέα τοῦ ποιμένος ἱλαρὰ ἦν λίαν, καὶ ἐν τοῖς προβάτοις περιέτρεχε.

translation:
  text: 'As I sat at home, I praised the Lord for everything I had seen. I thought about the commandments:
    they are good and powerful, they bring joy, they are glorious, and they can save a person’s soul.
    I said to myself, “I will be blessed if I follow these commandments, and everyone who follows them
    will be blessed.”


    While I was thinking about these things, I suddenly saw him sitting beside me. He said, “Why are you
    wavering about the commandments I gave you? They are good. Do not waver at all. Instead, clothe yourself
    with faith in the Lord, and you will follow them, for I will give you strength to do so.


    “These commandments help those who are ready to repent[a]. But if they do not live by them, their
    repentance is useless.


    “So, you who are turning away from your sins, throw off the evils of this age that wear you down.
    Clothe yourselves with every righteous virtue. Then you will be able to obey these commandments and
    stop adding to your sins. If you add no more sins, you will leave your former sins behind. Walk in
    these commandments of mine—follow them—and you will live for God. I have told you these things.”


    After he had finished speaking with me, he said, “Let us go out into the countryside, and I will show
    you the shepherds who tend the sheep.”


    “Let us go, sir,” I replied.


    We came to a plain, where he showed me a young shepherd. The young man was wearing a saffron-colored
    outfit.


    He was tending a very large flock of sheep. The sheep seemed to be living luxuriously and extravagantly.
    They were happy and leaped here and there. The shepherd was delighted with his flock. He looked extremely
    happy, and he ran about among the sheep.'
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    text: Repentance and related expressions are read in this works own context; they are not restricted
      to feeling sorry, and no uniform Godward formula is imposed. Use repentance for moral change while
      preserving the works own teaching about baptism, forgiveness, conduct and the angel of repentance;
      do not impose a different tradition on it.
    reason: lexical_alternative

base_translation:
  text: 'While I was sitting in my house and glorifying the Lord for all the things I had seen, and pondering
    the commandments—that they are good and powerful and gladdening and glorious and able to save a person’s
    soul—I said within myself: “Blessed shall I be if I walk in these commandments, and whoever walks
    in these will be blessed.”


    As I was saying these things within myself, I suddenly see him seated beside me and saying this: “Why
    are you double-minded about the commandments that I commanded you? They are good. Do not be double-minded
    at all, but clothe yourself with faith in the Lord, and you will walk in them; for I will strengthen
    you in them.


    “These commandments are beneficial for those who are about to repent[a]; for if they do not walk in
    them, their repentance is in vain.


    “You who are repenting, therefore, throw off the evils of this age that wear you down; and having
    put on every virtue of righteousness, you will be able to keep these commandments and no longer add
    to your sins. If, therefore, you add nothing further, you will be separated from your former sins.
    Walk, therefore, in these my commandments, and you will live to God. These things [all] have been
    spoken to you by me.”


    And after he had spoken these things with me, he says to me, “Let us go into a field, and I will show
    you the shepherds of the sheep.” “Let us go, sir,” I say. And we came to a certain plain, and he shows
    me a shepherd, a young man, clothed in a suit of garments, saffron in color.


    He was pasturing very many sheep, and the sheep were as if living in luxury and very self-indulgent,
    and they were cheerful, skipping here and there. And the shepherd himself was very cheerful over his
    flock; and the very appearance of the shepherd was exceedingly cheerful, and he ran around among the
    sheep.'
